# TerroirTrail — Independent Producer & Agritourism Guide

Canonical URL: https://terroir-trail.web.app/

## Current product state

TerroirTrail is an independent, discovery-first agritourism and producer guide. Its current audited catalogue spans Crete, Santorini, the Peloponnese, Northern Greece, and a Tuscany / Italy foothold. The same evidence-first rules apply across the catalogue: unknown facts stay unknown, public visitability is separate from partnership status, and location confidence is separate from road-access confidence.

The current audited bundled catalogue contains 62 producer/project records: 30 in Crete, 9 in Santorini, and 23 across the Peloponnese, Northern Greece and Tuscany / Italy. Current first-class producer categories include wineries, craft breweries, olive mills, olive-oil producers, dairies/cheesemakers, apiaries/honey producers, traditional distilleries/rakokazana, and farms.

Greek cheese and dairy expansion is now included in the audited catalogue. The implementation workstream retains 7 new dairy/cheese producer records in the bundled discovery and search catalogue alongside the two previously published dairy records, for 9 dairy records in total. Listings that could not meet the agreed exact persistent Google business-identity standard were removed rather than guessed. All 9 retained dairy records now carry persistent audited Google Place IDs. Exact location, visitability and road access remain independent trust dimensions; factory existence does not imply public tours or safe rental-car access.

TerroirTrail is not currently a public booking marketplace. Public visitability is researched separately from any TerroirTrail commercial relationship. A producer being publicly visitable does not mean that TerroirTrail is authorized to sell or reserve an Experience there.

## Discovery and contact

Travelers can:

- explore the audited catalogue on a map or list;
- search and filter producers/projects;
- open producer detail views with researched story, contact and visiting information;
- view live Google Places imagery only for manually audited listings with verified Google Place IDs, while keeping attribution visible;
- save favorites;
- use Terroir Passport stamps and personal notes;
- publish traveler ratings/reviews under the current account/community model;
- contact producers through public producer-controlled channels where available.

Unknown facts remain unknown. TerroirTrail does not invent ratings, prices, hospitality amenities, road conditions or booking availability to fill empty fields.

## Canonical producer discovery

TerroirTrail publishes canonical, crawlable producer entity pages at `/producers/<producer-id>/`. These pages are generated from the audited bundled catalogue used for deterministic deploy-time search/AEO output and offline fallback data. They expose source-backed identity, location, visitability and road-access facts without converting unknown data into positive claims.

Legacy `?producer=<id>` URLs are application deep links and should not be treated as the canonical producer entity URLs.

## Discovery Guides and navigation safety

TerroirTrail publishes Discovery Guides as verified-stop collections, not as road-safety guarantees.

The current audited guide set contains 10 published verified-stop Discovery Guides:

- Crete: four guides covering Heraklion wine country, Heraklion west, Western Chania, and a single-stop Rethymno olive-oil discovery guide.
- Santorini: three guides covering northern Santorini, the central/eastern producer cluster, and Megalochori/Pyrgos/caldera wine discovery.
- Phase 10B: three guides covering Nemea, a Northern Greece winery planner, and a single verified Monteraponi discovery stop in Tuscany.

Location confidence and road-access confidence are separate. Multi-stop driving navigation remains fail-closed wherever independent road-access evidence is incomplete. An individual map/location link identifies a place; it is not a guarantee that the approach road is suitable for a standard rental car.

## Santorini geological context

Santorini has major volcanic and geological significance, but TerroirTrail does not represent Santorini as a UNESCO Global Geopark. Geological heritage and formal UNESCO designation are kept separate.

## Experiences and bookings

TerroirTrail Experiences are not publicly populated without explicit producer agreement. Existing prototype/dormant Experience infrastructure must not be interpreted as a public offer.

No public TerroirTrail booking or tasting-reservation promise should be inferred from the current catalogue.

## Commercial features

Explorer Pass, Host Pro, chauffeur workflows and other commercial concepts are future/pilot functionality unless explicitly marked otherwise in the live product. They should not be described as generally available public products.

Third-party travel links, advertisements or affiliate links are separate from producer verification and do not affect TerroirTrail's editorial classification of a producer.

## Data principles

- Producer discovery and Experiences are separate layers.
- Public visitability does not equal TerroirTrail booking permission.
- Unknown data stays unknown.
- Unresolved coordinates are not guessed.
- Road access is only classified when supported by evidence.
- Google imagery is supplementary discovery media, not evidence of visitability, entrance precision or road safety.
- Producer/admin authority must be server-trusted rather than inferred from editable client profile fields.
- Geography remains open; no Greece-only architectural fence should be reintroduced.
- Search/AEO pages may reorganize verified information but must not manufacture facts or partnerships.

## Geographic scope

Current audited public catalogue:

- Crete, Greece — 30 audited records.
- Santorini, Greece — 9 audited records.
- Peloponnese, Northern Greece and Tuscany / Italy — 23 audited records combined.

The SEO, AEO and entity-discovery foundation includes the retained dairy expansion. New category and regional additions should follow the same evidence-first publication rules and be synchronized into both the live catalogue and deterministic deploy-time entity catalogue.
